texts: On day 111 of Year 1, Lantern-night fell.
Lantern-night is the longest night of the year.
The night was clear and very cold.
Every lantern in Aelmere was lit.
Meren Tallowhand lit the Stilllight Lantern at sundown as the speaker of the Council.
Every villager walked the Cliff Path at midnight from the harbor wall to the cliff-spires.
The cold wind blew strongly that night.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path held.
Joren Salt walked beside Meren Tallowhand.
The villagers told stories at the harbor fires until dawn.
Old Vesh told the story of the bad winter of sixty-three years ago.
Three sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.

q1_issues.issue: "Lantern-night fell" reifies no `fall` event at all — tense and the calendar terms are placed directly on the name symbol, which the instruction set licenses only for the light verbs occur / happen / take place, so the stated verb is dropped.

"the longest night **of the year**" drops the stated domain restriction, widening the superlative claim (the parallel `AmongMost` rule requires a stated domain restriction to stay on the entity as its own atoms).

"told stories" uses the bare kind filler `story`, but a bare-plural object taking part in an episodic past occurrence should mint an existential group witness per *Coordination & plurals*; the same filler is copied into the per-member rule.
"the story **of the bad winter**" loses its of-phrase entirely — no atom links sk_story_1 to sk_winter_1, so what the story was about is dropped.

q2_gaps: capacity / role adjunct "as the speaker of the Council" on an event — no licensed head for an in-what-capacity "as"-phrase, so the link between the capacity and the lighting event cannot be recorded
aboutness "of"-phrase on a non-nominalization noun ("the story of the bad winter") — explicitly excluded from `Possession` but never given a positive encoding
a time-period subject with an arrival verb ("Lantern-night fell") — the event-noun / light-verb rule names only occur / happen / take place
a domain restriction on a superlative ("the longest night of the year") — `Most` has no slot for the restricting domain
review.notes: One symbol `lantern_night` carries both the timeless kind claim ("is the longest night of the year") and the day-111 occurrence, conflating the recurring named night with that year's instance. `(Manner sk_blow_1 strongly)` is borderline between manner proper and the unslotted degree-adverb class.

issues.reason: "Night fell" predicates no falling — the literal reading is incoherent for a night — so putting the Day/Year terms and Past directly on the event-denoting lantern_night extends the light-verb rule's own rationale (the event-noun's witness IS the eventuality), and every atom emitted is true of the sentence and well-typed; the reviewer's own q2 gap concedes the construction is uncovered.

The standing half is the gap the reviewer also files — Most's third slot is the comparison class and has no room for a restricting domain, so "of the year" goes unrecorded; the widening charge does not stand, since night is exactly the head-noun class the superlative rule puts in that slot and, for a recurring annual night, "of the year" names the comparison cycle rather than carving out a narrower set, so no false or over-asserted atom is emitted.

*Coordination & plurals* states that a bare-plural object in an episodic clause takes an existential group witness when the set takes part in the occurrence, reserving the bare kind filler for non-specific / kind-level objects ("pays tax", "grows wheat"), and "the villagers told stories at the harbor fires until dawn" is a one-off dated occurrence — so (Theme sk_tell_1 story), copied again into the per-member rule, is the storage the instruction set reserves for the other case.

The loss is real — nothing links sk_story_1 to sk_winter_1, so the winter's atoms dangle and the sentence's aboutness is unrecorded — but calling it a parse defect overstates it: an about-of-phrase on a non-derived noun is barred from Possession and given no positive encoding anywhere (the Of oblique is stated only for nominalizations' objects and for position/origin), and every atom the parse did emit is true and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: Capacity/role "as"-phrase on an event ("lit ... as the speaker of the Council") — no licensed head ties the capacity to the event.
Aboutness "of"-phrase on a non-nominalization noun ("the story of the bad winter") — excluded from Possession, never given a positive encoding.
A time-period subject with an arrival verb ("Lantern-night fell") — the light-verb rule names only occur / happen / take place.
A domain restriction on a superlative ("the longest night of the year") — Most has no slot for the restricting domain.
new_gaps: A named recurring night/period gets one stable name symbol reused for every mention (*Names and casing*), so the type-level claim (Most long lantern_night night) and a single occurrence's atoms ((Past lantern_night), (Time lantern_night (Day 111))) collide on one symbol — nothing licenses separating the recurring named event from that year's instance, and (Past lantern_night) reads as false of the recurring night.

The entity-attached surface-preposition oblique is the obvious carrier for an aboutness of-phrase ((Of sk_story_1 sk_winter_1)), but that open licence is stated only for position/origin prepositions and for nominalizations' objects; extending it explicitly to non-derived nouns would close the "story of the bad winter" gap.
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 2: the compliant form mints an existential group witness for the bare-plural object — (GroupOf sk_stories_1 story) with (Theme sk_tell_1 sk_stories_1) on the group event, and a per-binding Skolem group inside the distribution rule ((GroupOf (sk_stories $x) story), (Theme (sk_tell $x) (sk_stories $x))) — the bare kind symbol story being reserved for non-specific / kind-level objects.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the parse is strong: "that night" resolved by term propagation onto Day 111 / Year 1, the three universals rendered as restriction-in-premise rules with their companions, and the sky-cats' state distributed as per-member Skolem states instead of riding the group symbol. (Manner sk_blow_1 strongly) is manner proper (how the wind blew), not the unslotted degree-adverb class, so it needs no flag.
